articles.title: Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
articles.summary: The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from Chicago, where communities are battling a new wave of synthetic drugs.
articles.body:
Warning: This video contains descriptions of drug-taking and distressing images

A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump pledged a crackdown on drug cartels, proscribing many as terrorist organisations.

Drug overdose deaths have fallen from a peak of around 110,000 in 2022, down to roughly 70,000 last year.

However, America's decades-long drug crisis may be accelerating and authorities are increasingly concerned about cheaper, more powerful synthetic drugs, including an animal tranquilliser called tranq.

The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from the frontlines in South Side, Chicago, where communities are battling the crisis.

articles.title: How will Europe deal with youth-led protests?
articles.summary: Demonstrations are spreading across the continent.
articles.body:
Weeks of student protests in France have grown into some of the worst unrest in Europe in recent years.

The demonstrations started as a call for reforms to the education system. But they have since expanded into protests against the high cost of living and planned cuts to social services.

And France is not alone. Demonstrators have taken to the streets in other parts of Europe. They are venting their frustrations against leaders they say have failed to address their needs, and putting pressure on their governments.

And right-wing parties are looking to seize the moment to make political gains.

articles.title: Ato pró-Lula em João Pessoa reúne apoiadores no Mercado de Mangabeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Mobilização começou por volta das 15h e foi convocada pelas redes sociais. Manifestantes e apoiadores carregaram cartazes e faixas em apoio a reeleição de Lula.
articles.summary: Ato pró-Lula em João Pessoa reuniu manifestantes com faixas e cartazes no Mercado de Mangabeira em mobilização convocada pelas redes sociais para o segundo turno.
articles.body:
Apoiadores realizam ato pró-Lula no Mercado Público de Mangabeira, em João Pessoa — Foto: Débora Luz/TV Cabo Branco

Apoiadores realizaram na tarde deste domingo (18) um ato em apoio ao presidente Lula (PT), no Mercado Público de Mangabeira, na capital paraibana João Pessoa .

A mobilização começou por volta das 15h e foi convocada pelas redes sociais. Manifestantes e apoiadores carregaram cartazes e faixas em apoio à reeleição de Lula.

Apoiadores políticos de Lula na Paraíba, como o governador reeleito Lucas Ribeiro (PP), o senador João Azevêdo (PSB) e a deputada estadual reeleita Cida Ramos (PT), marcaram presença no ato. A deputada federal de Minas Gerais, Ana Elisa (PT), também participou do evento.

O segundo turno das Eleições 2026 acontece no próximo domingo (25). No primeiro turno, Lula obteve 45,16% dos votos válidos, e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ficou na liderança, com 47,03%.

articles.title: Pescador encontra corpo de mulher no mar de Itanhaém | G1
articles.standfirst: Corpo foi localizado próximo à Laje da Conceição e retirado da água pelo Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar). Pescador disse que permaneceu no local até a chegada dos agentes.
articles.summary: Corpo foi localizado próximo à Laje da Conceição e retirado da água pelo Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar).
articles.body:
Mulher foi encontrada no mar de Itanhaém (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

Uma mulher, de 43 anos, foi encontrada morta no mar de Itanhaém , no litoral de São Paulo. Conforme apurado pelo g1 , a vítima foi identificada como a turista que havia desaparecido em um rio de Peruíbe, cidade vizinha.

O corpo foi localizado por um pescador esportivo próximo da Laje da Conceição nesta sexta-feira (16). Ao g1 , o pescador, que preferiu não se identificar, informou que demorou para acreditar no que viu e ficou abalado com a cena, mas permaneceu por perto até a chegada dos bombeiros.

“Quero acreditar que Deus me colocou nessa situação para entregar o corpo para a família”, afirmou o pescador, acrescentando acreditar que os familiares mereciam uma despedida.

De acordo com o Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar), os profissionais realizaram a retirada do corpo da água e o desembarque na região da Boca da Barra. A ação contou com três viaturas e seis bombeiros guarda-vidas.

Ainda segundo a corporação, o marido da vítima reconheceu o corpo da mulher neste sábado (17). Ela morava em Salesópolis (SP).

Segundo o GBMar, a corporação foi acionada na tarde de sábado (11) após o relato de que uma moradora de Salesópolis (SP) havia desaparecido nas águas do Rio Guaraú.

As equipes foram até o local e realizaram buscas na desembocadura do rio e no mar. No entanto, a operação foi encerrada sem localizar a vítima por conta da perda da visibilidade no local.

Apesar disso, as buscas foram retomadas nos dias seguintes, sem sucesso.

Caso ocorreu no Rio Guaraú, em Peruíbe — Foto: Edison Baraçal/Arquivo A Tribuna Jornal

articles.title: Incêndio atinge vegetação de campus do ITA Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Com previsão para início de aulas em 2027, novo campus da instituição teve primeiras instalações inauguradas em abril deste ano e obras continuam.
articles.summary: Com previsão para início de aulas em 2027, novo campus da instituição teve primeiras instalações inauguradas em abril deste ano e obras continuam.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu uma área de vegetação dentro do terreno do campus do Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica (ITA) do Ceará , na Base Aérea de Fortaleza , neste domingo (18).

O fogo teria atingido vegetação próxima ao muro que fica na BR-116. Portanto, o local do canteiro de obras e prédios já construídos não teriam sido atingidos. Motoristas que passaram pelo local durante esta tarde registraram o momento em que as chamas atingiam o local.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado via Coordenadoria Integrada de Operações de Segurança (CIOPS) por volta de 13h38 e enviou equipes ao local.

O incêndio foi contido ainda na tarde deste domingo . Os bombeiros informaram que por volta das 15h38 a ocorrência estava concluída.

Incêndio no campus do ITA Ceará — Foto: Reprodução

A primeira sede do Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica (ITA) fora de São José dos Campos (SP), o ITA Ceará, será instalada na Base Aérea de Fortaleza, no bairro Aeroporto. No dia 1º de abril de 2026, houve a inauguração da primeira etapa das obras em cerimônia com a presença do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Foram inaugurados dois prédios, que serão o bloco das engenharias e do alojamento estudantil. Os prédios estão em fase de acabamento. O espaço terá 14 laboratórios e 40 quartos com sala de estar e cozinha, com capacidade para 80 alunos.

📚 Anunciado em 2023, o campus avançado do ITA no Ceará será a segunda unidade do Instituto e a primeira fora da cidade de São José dos Campos (SP) nos 75 anos de história do instituto.

Ao todo, houve um investimento de R$ 445,4 milhões no ITA Ceará , de acordo com o Governo Federal. O início das atividades acadêmicas está previsto para 2027. Ele abrigará dois novos cursos estratégicos , que não são lecionados na sede de São Paulo: engenharia de energia e engenharia de sistemas.

O bloco para os cursos de engenharia terá três pavimentos, com:

Espaço para professores, bibliotecas e eventos

Já o bloco de alojamento estudantil terá:

2 quartos com acessibilidade (capacidade para 4 alunos)

40 quartos com sala de estar e cozinha (capacidade para 80 alunos)

O primeiro processo seletivo de acesso ao ITA Ceará aconteceu em 2024, com a primeira turma sendo acolhida em 2025 e 2026 ainda no campus de São José dos Campos, em São Paulo. Após a conclusão das obras, as turmas serão transferidas à nova unidade, no Ceará, para dar prosseguimento às atividades. A previsão para o início das atividades é 2027.

O ITA tem seis tradicionais cursos de Engenharia: Aeronáutica, Eletrônica, Mecânica-Aeronáutica, Civil-Aeronáutica, Computação e Aeroespacial.

No ITA Ceará, foram acrescentados dois novos cursos: Engenharia de Sistemas e Engenharia de Energias Renováveis , com perspectiva de cursos de pós-graduação e de outra oferta de graduação em Bioengenharia.

Para a nova sede do Instituto, 99 servidores foram aprovados em concurso público , incluindo professores, pesquisadores, técnicos e tecnologistas. Desses, 33 já tomaram posse e estão trabalhando na implementação das atividades que serão realizadas no campus.

O prédio do ITA Ceará foi projetado pela Lins Arquitetos, um escritório cearense, com base no Cariri.

articles.title: Trump diz que não quer afastar Rússia de negociações e acusa Zelensky de prolongar guerra | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA justificou a suspensão de sanções e tarifas contra Moscou como forma de preservar as negociações de paz e criticou ataques ucranianos a refinarias russas, alegando impacto no mercado de diesel.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA justificou a suspensão de sanções e tarifas contra Moscou como forma de preservar as negociações de paz e criticou ataques ucranianos a refinarias russas, alegando impacto no mercado de diesel.
articles.body:
Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump e Volodymyr Zelensky. — Foto: Sputnik/Gavriil Grigorov/Pool via REUTERS, Reuters e Genya Savilov/AFP

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , afirmou neste domingo (18) que não quer adotar medidas que afastem a Rússia das negociações para encerrar a guerra na Ucrânia.

Em publicação na rede social Truth Social, ele voltou a justificar a suspensão de sanções e tarifas contra Moscou e criticou o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky , a quem acusou de não querer acabar com o conflito.

Trump afirmou que sua decisão sobre as medidas contra a Rússia "é simples" porque seu governo está tentando negociar a paz. Segundo ele, assinar a legislação que prevê as sanções neste momento poderia prejudicar as conversas.

"Minha decisão sobre a Rússia é muito simples. Estou em processo de negociação da paz na guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia e não quero fazer nada que, de maneira insensata, afaste a Rússia da mesa de negociações. Grandes avanços estão sendo feitos, e isso inclui as atuais negociações sobre reféns!"

O presidente também disse que poderá assinar o documento mais adiante, sem estabelecer uma data para uma eventual mudança de posição.

A declaração ocorre depois de Trump suspender, na sexta-feira (16), a aplicação de sanções e tarifas previstas na chamada Lei Graham . As medidas deveriam entrar em vigor na semana seguinte e incluíam tarifas sobre produtos russos e penalidades a países que compram petróleo e gás da Rússia.

No sábado (17), o secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, afirmou que Trump pretende usar um período de até 60 dias para avaliar os efeitos econômicos das medidas . Segundo Rubio, a análise considera possíveis impactos tanto sobre a economia global quanto sobre a dos EUA.

Trump publicou nas redes sociais uma justificativa para sua decisão sobre as sanções à Rússia. — Foto: Reprodução/Truth Social

Trump critica Zelensky e ataques a refinarias russas

Na publicação deste domingo, Trump criticou os ataques ucranianos a refinarias de diesel na Rússia e afirmou que eles prejudicam o mercado internacional do combustível, com impactos sobre empresas e produtores americanos.

O presidente, porém, não apresentou dados que permitam dimensionar os efeitos mencionados.

"Zelensky está usando refinarias de diesel na Rússia como alvo, sabendo que esses ataques estão prejudicando seriamente os mercados mundiais de diesel, inclusive nos EUA. Agricultores, pecuaristas e empresas de todos os tipos estão sofrendo muito com isso, mas a Rússia, apesar disso, está enviando milhões de barris de diesel ao mundo a preços baixos."

Trump também acusou Zelensky de não querer encerrar a guerra e afirmou que o presidente ucraniano poderia ter conseguido um acordo melhor anos atrás. Na mesma publicação, mencionou o apoio financeiro dado à Ucrânia por países europeus e pelo governo do ex-presidente americano Joe Biden.

Zelensky, por sua vez, criticou a suspensão das sanções e alertou que a medida poderia fortalecer o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, e prolongar o conflito.

Suspensão de sanções e acordo sobre diesel

A suspensão das sanções contra a Rússia ocorre em meio à preocupação do governo americano com os efeitos dos conflitos internacionais sobre o fornecimento de energia.

No sábado, o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, afirmou que a guerra na Ucrânia e os confrontos no Oriente Médio afetam o abastecimento global e defendeu um acordo para ampliar a oferta de diesel russo nos mercados internacionais.

Segundo Trump, a Rússia forneceria inicialmente mais de 300 mil toneladas métricas do combustível aos EUA, com novas remessas previstas a partir de novembro.

O secretário de Energia americano, Chris Wright, afirmou neste domingo que o acordo busca incentivar o fim da guerra, e não oferecer apoio econômico à Rússia. Segundo ele, o aumento das exportações russas de diesel dependeria de uma redução do conflito com a Ucrânia.

articles.title: Filho de confeitaria que morreu com câncer raro exalta força da mãe | G1
articles.standfirst: Morte de Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares, de 45 anos, causou comoção nas redes sociais entre familiares e amigos. Ela foi lembrada como uma mulher guerreira.
articles.summary: Morte de Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares, de 45 anos, causou comoção nas redes sociais entre familiares e amigos. Ela foi lembrada como uma mulher guerreira.
articles.body:
A chef de confeitaria Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares, de 45 anos, que morreu durante o tratamento de um câncer raro , recebeu homenagens nas redes sociais. Em seu perfil, o filho Iago Calixto exaltou a força da mãe por enfrentar a doença com um sorriso no rosto.

"Você foi a pessoa mais forte que conheci e passou por tudo com um sorriso no rosto. Descanse em paz, minha mãe. Eu te amo para sempre", escreveu.

Veri morreu no sábado (17). A confeiteira lutava contra a doença desde julho de 2025, quando recebeu o diagnóstico de carcinoma adenoescamoso de colo uterino metastático, uma forma agressiva de câncer cervical.

Ela era proprietária da Veri Pires Confeitaria Artesanal, onde produzia bolos caseiros e sobremesas por encomenda. Os pedidos haviam sido temporariamente suspensos em razão da doença.

"Hoje nos despedimos de uma verdadeira guerreira, mas acima de tudo, de uma testemunha viva da fé. A sua jornada contra o câncer não foi definida pela doença, mas sim pela garra extraordinária com que enfrentou cada dia", destacou uma amiga.

Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Veri Pires

Nas redes sociais, a confeiteira costumava compartilhar informações sobre a doença, o tratamento e a recuperação, além de demonstrar a fé na cura em momentos de oração com a família.

"Pausa para a cura. Lutando contra um tipo raro de câncer. Compartilho meu processo com fé, coragem e propósito", diz a biografia do perfil dela no Instagram.

Natural de Caldas Novas, Veri viveu por um período em Gramado, no Rio Grande do Sul, antes de retornar à cidade natal.

articles.title: Chuva causa transtornos e deixa desalojados no extremo sul da Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporal começou durante a noite de sábado (17) e segue em alguns pontos neste domingo (18). Há uma alerta de tempestade do Inmet para a região.
articles.summary: Temporal começou durante a noite de sábado (17) e segue em alguns pontos da região neste domingo (18). Há uma alerta de tempestade do Inmet para a região
articles.body:
O temporal que atingiu o extremo sul da Bahia neste fim de semana causou transtornos para as populações de pelo menos três cidades da região: Itamaraju , Porto Seguro e Medeiros Neto .

Todas estão na lista dos 193 municípios com alerta para tempestade , divulgado pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).

Entre a noite de sábado (17) e este domingo (18), foram registrados casos de alagamentos, desabamentos e quedas de árvores, entre outras ocorrências.

Segundo as respectivas prefeituras e órgãos de controle de danos, pelo menos seis pessoas ficaram desalojadas e duas feridas nessas situações. (Confira os detalhes abaixo)

Vídeos compartilhados nas redes sociais mostram os estragos. Em um deles, é possível ver o momento em que uma árvore cai sobre uma barraca de bebidas. (Assista acima)

Chuva causa estragos no extremo sul da Bahia — Foto: Redes Sociais

Em Itamaraju, segunda a Defes Civil, foram registradas ocorrências como desabamento de muros e alagamentos. Apesar do susto, ninguém ficou ferido.

Ao todo, seis pessoas ficaram desalojadas nessas situação. Elas foram abrigados nas casas de familiares, que também moram no município.

Somente na noite de sábado, a estimativa do acumulado de chuvas é de 14 mm. Neste domingo, o temoral segue atingido a cidade.

Na cidade de Porto Seguro, conforme informou a Defesa Civil, foram registradas três ocorrências distintas envolvendo queda de árvores, com danos a estruturas comerciais e residenciais, pessoas feridas e situação de risco à segurança da população.

Uma das ocorrências foi no distritito de Trancosco, um dos principais destinos turísticos do estado. Moradores observavam a chuva, na noite do sábado, quando galhos de uma árvore caiu sobre uma barraca. Uma testemunha filmou o momento exato do acidente. (Assista acima)

Pelo menos duas pessoas ficaram feridas no momento. Segundo o órgão, há relato de uma vítima com possível fratura no braço, que estava ainda em atendimento hospitalar.

Em outro ponto do distrito, uma família ficou desabrigadas após a queda de outra árvore sobre uma casa. Entre os residentes, estão duas crianças, de 10 e 4 anos.

A família foi encaminhada para o Centro de Referência de Assistência Social (CRAS) para atendimento e avaliação quanto à concessão do benefício de aluguel social, conforme os critérios estabelecidos pelo município.

O levantamento dos prejuízos permanece em andamento, com a equipe da Defesa Civil buscando contato com os comerciantes afetados.

Chuva causa estragos em Medeiros Neto, no extremo sul da Bahia — Foto: Redes Sociais

Já em Medeiros Neto, além da chuva, moradores enfrentaram ventania e granizo. Vídeos feitos por testemunhas mostram os danos causados pelo temporal.

Conforme a prefeitura, durante aproximadamente 30 minutos, uma forte chuva, acompanhada de ventos intensos, arrancou telhados e portões, derrubou muros e paredes de residências e deixou algumas casas completamente destelhadas.

Galhos de árvores foram quebrados e carregados pelo vento, assim como tampas de caixas-d’água e antenas parabólicas. A rede elétrica também foi afetada e parte da cidade ficou sem energia elétrica.

Algumas ruas permanecem interditadas devido à queda de fios na via, como medida de segurança para evitar acidentes.

Apesar de todos os estragos, não há registro de pessoas feridas. Essas são as primeiras informações que conseguimos repassar.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Medeiros Neto, por meio da Secretaria de Assistência Social, informou que ainda está contabilizando as famílias atingidas. Até o momento, poucas precisaram deixar suas casas para se abrigar na residência de familiares.

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3071: Apostas de Sergipe ganham prêmios; veja cidades | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogos foram registrados em nove municípios sergipanos e por canais eletrônicos da Caixa. Não houve ganhadores da sena neste concurso, e próximo sorteio pode pagar até R$ 185 milhões.
articles.summary: Com prêmio acumulado em R$ 185 milhões, Mega-Sena 3071 premia 31 apostas de Sergipe que acertaram a quadra em nove municípios e canais eletrônicos.
articles.body:
Trinta e uma apostas feitas em Sergipe acertaram quatro números e foram premiadas na quadra no sorteio do concurso 3071 da Mega-Sena , realizado na manhã deste domingo (18).

O maior valor do estado foi para Aracaju , onde um bolão com sete números faturou R$ 4.018,60. As demais 30 apostas acertaram quatro dezenas e ganharam R$ 1.339,55 cada. Entre os jogos premiados com este valor, dois tiveram a opção de teimosinha ativada: um registrado na capital e outro em São Miguel do Aleixo.

Os prêmios foram distribuídos em nove municípios sergipanos, além dos canais digitais da Caixa Econômica Federal.

Não houve ganhadores da sena neste concurso, e próximo sorteio pode pagar até R$ 185 milhões.

Veja os números sorteados : 12 - 22 - 51 - 52 - 41 - 45.

Aracaju: 20 apostas ganhadoras (19 jogos simples e 1 bolão).

Nossa Senhora do Socorro: 2 apostas simples.

Frei Paulo : 1 aposta simples (canal digital).

Nossa Senhora da Glória : 1 aposta simples.

Poço Verde: 1 aposta simples (canal digital).

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

Volantes da Mega-Sena — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer / Agência Brasil

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online . Para concorrer, é necessário ter mais que 18 anos de idade.

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

articles.title: Brasileiro de 14 anos é premiado em Londres por redação internacional | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedro Henrique Vaz Negrini, de Uberlândia (MG), recebeu reconhecimento do John Locke Institute, em Londres, e também ganhou uma bolsa de US$ 1 mil para cursos universitários.
articles.summary: Pedro Henrique, de Uberlândia, conquistou prêmio do John Locke Institute e bolsa de estudos após redação com referências a Graciliano Ramos e Legião Urbana.
articles.body:
O jeans e a camiseta deram lugar à gravata borboleta, ao sapato social e ao smoking. Foi assim que Pedro Henrique Vaz Negrini, de 14 anos, morador de Uberlândia , recebeu em Londres um reconhecimento internacional por seu ensaio no Global Essay Prize 2026.

O estudante já se considerava vitorioso por estar entre os selecionados do concurso, que recebeu trabalhos de 100.237 participantes de 183 países . Mas ele foi além: em 3 de outubro, durante a cerimônia de gala em Londres, recebeu um certificado de 'Alta Recomendação' (High Recommendation), concedido pelo John Locke Institute.

"Eu não esperava estar entre os premiados. Quando anunciaram meu nome levei um susto e demorei alguns instantes para entender o que estava acontecendo. A 'High Recommendation', o que me colocava no top 7 da minha categoria ".

Pedro conta que, naquele momento, se lembrou de toda a trajetória até ali e ficou feliz ao perceber que havia chegado mais longe do que imaginava. Para ele, a recomendação do John Locke Institute representa o reconhecimento de um período de dedicação aos estudos.

Além do certificado, Pedro Henrique recebeu uma bolsa de US$ 1 mil para utilizar em cursos oferecidos pelo instituto. As opções incluem programas em locais como Oxford, Cambridge, Dubai e Washington.

Ele participou da categoria Júnior de Relações Internacionais, que propôs aos candidatos a seguinte pergunta: “A ajuda externa beneficia ou prejudica os pobres?”.

Pedro Henrique e o pai, Érico Negrini, em noite de Gala promovida pelo John Locke Institute, em Londres — Foto: Divulgação

A programação do John Locke Institute ocorreu nos dias 2 e 4 de outubro, em dois hotéis de Londres. Os finalistas também tiveram a chance de conhecer a Vila do instituto, um espaço para os jovens de diferentes culturas se conhecerem e trocarem ideias.

Em parte da programação, Pedro foi acompanhado pelo pai, Érico Negrini, e por Júlio Abdalla, mantenedor do Colégio Gabarito, onde o estudante cursa o 9º ano.

Um dos momentos marcantes da viagem foi receber um convite para um café da manhã na residência oficial do embaixador do Brasil no Reino Unido. Na ocasião, eles conversaram com Antonio Patriota sobre o prêmio, temas atuais de geopolítica e o trabalho da diplomacia brasileira.

Pedro disse que conhecer estudantes de diferentes partes do mundo também foi um dos destaques da viagem. Durante o evento de premiação, ele dividiu a mesa com participantes da Índia, do Paquistão e da China. Em inglês, conversou com eles sobre a rotina e as expectativas para o futuro.

"Alguns deles já estudam fora, construindo uma trajetória internacional e percebi como o conhecimento pode aproximar pessoas de culturas muito diferentes e ampliar nossos horizontes. É um caminho que sonho em seguir".

Pedro Henrique voltou para casa com uma premiação, novos contatos, amizades e aprendizados.

Durante a noite de gala em Londres, Pedro conta que entrou 'em clima de jornalista' e 'entrevistou' participantes de outros países. Entre eles estavam uma estudante de Hong Kong e um britânico que escreveu um ensaio sobre o revolucionário marxista Che Guevara.

Para Pedro, o prêmio representa uma conquista pessoal e reforça sua confiança de que a dedicação, a curiosidade e a disposição para enfrentar desafios podem abrir oportunidades.

Pedro pretende continuar participando de olimpíadas do conhecimento e mantém o sonho de estudar em uma universidade como o Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts (Massachusetts Institute of Technology, MIT), nos Estados Unidos.

"Eu sei que essa premiação do John Locke Institute, isoladamente, não me garante uma vaga no MIT, mas com certeza é uma conquista significativa no caminho até lá".

Durante o evento, foi anunciado que a cerimônia de premiação de 2027 será realizada em Paris. Pedro já se prepara para participar novamente.

"Com certeza vou participar novamente, e quem sabe ter a chance de representar Uberlândia e o Brasil nesse cenário internacional. Mais do que ganhar medalhas ou prêmios, quero novas oportunidades para crescer".

Pedro Henrique e o pai em Abbey Road — Foto: Divulgação

O ensaio de Pedro Henrique reuniu referências da filosofia, da literatura e da música. Entre as obras que ele leu estão 'Os que se afastam de Omelas', de Ursula K. Le Guin, textos do filósofo John Rawls e 'Vidas Secas', de Graciliano Ramos.

Na música, ele se inspirou em 'Geração Coca-Cola', da Legião Urbana, e 'A Novidade', de Gilberto Gil, na versão gravada pelos Paralamas do Sucesso.

Natural de Brasília, Pedro mora com a família em Uberlândia há um ano. O pai é fã da Legião Urbana e, com o tempo, o estudante também desenvolveu carinho pela banda liderada por Renato Russo, que morreu em 1996. As letras do grupo abordam questões sociais e seguem despertando reflexões entre diferentes gerações.

"Admiro a profundidade das letras e a forma como elas ainda dialogam com diferentes gerações. Por mais que esse ensaio não tenha sido escrito pensando em uma homenagem musical, espero que seja recebido com carinho por fãs da Legião Urbana".

Pedro também é fã dos Beatles e aproveitou a viagem a Londres para conhecer a famosa faixa de pedestres da Abbey Road, eternizada na capa de um dos álbuns da banda.

"Como todo fã dos Beatles eu fiz questão de estar na calçada do Abbey Road, onde eles gravaram o álbum de 1969 que imortalizou aquela faixa em frente ao estúdio".

Pedro Henrique disse que no começo, estar entre os finalistas parecia um sonho distante — Foto: Divulgação

Pedro Henrique contou com a orientação do professor Alisson Júnio Parreira Peixoto, que identificou potencial no estudante e o incentivou a dar o primeiro passo.

Pedro afirma que voltou de Londres mais confiante e grato, com vontade de compartilhar o que aprendeu. Para ele, estar na cidade cosmopolita abriu novos horizontes. O jovem pretende participar novamente do concurso, mas quer incentivar outros estudantes a também desenvolverem seus projetos.

"Voltei de Londres com a ideia de formar um grupo para ajudar outros estudantes a desenvolverem seus projetos. Sei que temos muitos por aí com ideias maravilhosas e interessantes e só precisam de um lugar, um espaço para falar sobre elas".

Durante o tempo livre Pedro Henrique visitou várias regiões de Londres — Foto: Divulgação

O g1 procurou o John Locke Institute para saber como tem sido a participação de brasileiros no concurso, criado em 2019, e qual é a presença de adolescentes de países em desenvolvimento, como o Brasil. A instituição não respondeu até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Motociclista morre na Rodovia do Açúcar em Piracicaba após colisão | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu no KM 157 da pista na madruga deste domingo (18). Ocupantes dos carros envolvidos não sofreram ferimentos, segundo informou concessionária.
articles.summary: Motociclista morre na Rodovia do Açúcar em Piracicaba após ser atingido na traseira por carro que fugiu do local no KM 157 na madrugada deste domingo.
articles.body:
Rodovia do Açúcar (SP-308) na região de Piracicaba — Foto: Divulgação/Rodovias do Tietê

Um motociclista morreu após ser atingido por um carro na Rodovia do Açúcar (SP-308), em Piracicaba (SP), na madrugada deste domingo (18). Com o impacto, a vítima foi arremessada para o canteiro central da pista, segundo informações da concessionária Rodovias do Tietê, responsável pelo trecho.

Os ocupantes dos carros não sofreram ferimentos. O acidente ocorreu no Km 157 acidente foi no km 157. O motocicleta foi atingida na traseira pelo carro que seguia na pista.

Ainda conforme informações da concessionária, um segundo veículo também bateu contra a moto.

O primeiro carro, que bateu contra a moto, fugiu do local do acidente, aponta registro da concessionária.

Uma das faixas da Rodovia do Açúcar precisou ser interditada durante a madrugada para atendimento das vítimas. O trecho foi liberado por volta das 4h deste domingo.

articles.title: 'The Chosen' actor endorses James Talarico, claims candidate reflects real 'Christian values'
articles.summary: Jordan Walker Ross of "The Chosen" backs James Talarico's Texas Senate bid, sparking a fierce clash over film incentives and faith politics.
articles.body: 'The Chosen' actor Jordan Walker Ross endorsed Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico on Thursday, helping launch a faith-based voter coalition ahead of November's election while drawing criticism from a Republican state lawmaker over taxpayer-funded Hollywood subsidies. Ross, who portrays the apostle Little James in the popular faith-based television series, announced his endorsement in a campaign video promoting "Faithful Texans for Talarico," an initiative intended to attract religious voters. "A lot of politicians like to talk about Christian values, but you don’t really see that reflected in their legislation or the way that they live, but you do see that in the way that James lives. He loves his neighbor; he takes care of the needy, the sick, the immigrant," Ross said. A spokesperson for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton's campaign slammed Talarico's appeals to Christian voters in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing the Democrat of using his religious beliefs to justify progressive positions on social issues. 'OFFICE' STAR SAYS JAMES TALARICO'S RELIGIOUS BELIEFS 'ACHINGLY CLOSE' TO JESUS CHRIST "Everything about James Talarico is fake," the spokesperson said. "He uses his beliefs to justify his most radical positions, all while calling himself ‘a Christian who hates Christianity.’ In Talarico’s twisted version of Christianity, a follower of Christ is required to bend the knee at thealtar of the radical trans agenda, disavow the oil and gas industry, support late-term abortion, and open the door to every criminal illegal immigrant seeking asylum. I’m still looking through the Bible to find those passages, but I wouldn’t call it Christian." Texas state Rep. Brian Harrison, R-Texas, also criticized the endorsement on X, accusing state lawmakers of subsidizing actors who support Democrats. "Your money is being used to help elect Democrats like James Talarico," he said. Harrison also took aim at Texas Senate Bill 22, which expanded Texas' film incentive program. Texas Film Commission records show that The Chosen Texas LLC received approximately $862,527 for its second season in 2022 and another $1.995 million for its fourth season in March 2025, totaling near $2.86 million. Both payments preceded the new legislation's September 2025 effective date. In a follow-up statement to Fox News Digital, Harrison slammed the film program as a "socialist scheme to give billions of tax dollars to rich, woke, Hollywood leftists." He argued that production offsets "directly or indirectly" subsidize actor salaries, pledging to introduce legislation next session to repeal the "indefensible" Hollywood subsidies. NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS Ross defended the film incentives and rejected the suggestion that actors' political endorsements should affect production opportunities. "The growing film industry in TX creates thousands of jobs for Texans who fall on both sides of the aisle," Ross said, in a statement Sunday to Fox News Digital. "For Harrison to suggest that those opportunities should be taken away simply because some actors — like myself — endorse Democratic candidates is unconstitutional. One of the beautiful things about our country is the right to voice our opinions and I encourage my fellow actors/filmmakers (on the right AND left) to do the same." "I believe it’s time for a change and that James Talarico offers a clear vision for how to create those changes," he continued. COWBOYS LEGEND RANDY WHITE ENDORSES KEN PAXTON, WARNS JAMES TALARICO ‘CAN’T BE TRUSTED’ Brittany Hughes, a video host at the Media Research Center, criticized Ross' endorsement in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing that his role as an apostle on "The Chosen" did not make him an authority on Christian teachings. "As is any American, Ross is free to vote for whatever candidate he chooses," she said. "But American voters aren’t obligated to take a theological lesson from an actor simply because he plays an apostle on TV." "It’s a simple fact that many of Talarico’s public positions are in total opposition to basic Christian principles — his support for so-called gender transitioning, for example, which is completely at odds with the biblical description of God having created us male and female separately and for separate purposes," she added. TALARICO DISMISSES PAST COMMENTS ABOUT GOD AND GENDER AS 'PROVOCATIVE' WHILE INVOKING CHARLIE KIRK Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't L.A. My Burbank PAC, criticized the endorsement in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning whether Hollywood actors could influence Texas voters. "I highly doubt this will help Talarico with voters, but Ross’ outspoken progressive politics could alienate Christian audiences from The Chosen. Christians and Texas voters can see through this kind of set piece Christianity," she said. "Theater kids generally make terrible political pundits." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Ross rejected the idea that political differences necessarily alienate fans, saying he welcomes conversations with viewers who disagree with him. "As a progressive actor on a TV show with a largely conservative audience, I’ve had so many wonderful opportunities to engage in challenging conversations with my fans and I also do so from a place of compassion and curiosity. When we do that, we can learn so much from one another." Fox News Digital reached out to Talarico and the Texas Film Commission for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: Homan says Ilhan Omar could be stripped of naturalization, deported if immigration fraud is proven
articles.summary: Border czar Tom Homan says Ilhan Omar could face denaturalization and deportation if it is confirmed she committed immigration fraud.
articles.body: Border czar Tom Homan said Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., could be denaturalized and deported if investigators find that she committed immigration fraud, repeating his assertion that no one is above the law after her home was raided and cellphone seized. "Of course, if you lie during the naturalization process, there is a process to denaturalize somebody. We've done it before... And certainly, if the evidence points that way, that could happen," Homan told "The Big Weekend Show" on Saturday. Omar will "be held to the same standards you and I are held [to]. If she violated the law, then she'll be held accountable," he added, declining to discuss the specifics of the investigation into the congresswoman. "I said over a year ago, the allegations were made clear, and it would be investigated, and they are investigating it," he said. "I'm not going to get ahead of the bureau or HSI, but I've been told they have a strong case, and we'll let the evidence lead where it leads." Omar is under federal investigation over allegations that she or her father lied about her birth year on immigration paperwork to obtain her citizenship when her family fled Somalia in the late 1990s. DEMOCRATS' FURY OVER ILHAN OMAR RAID DRAWS STINGING GOP REMINDER ABOUT RAID FROM THE PAST: ‘SET THE PRECEDENT’ Her father became a U.S. citizen in 2000. Omar was believed to be 17 at the time, and, as a minor, automatically qualified for citizenship under U.S. law along with him. But, recently, it’s been alleged she was actually 18 and would have needed to go through the process herself at that point. Omar and other Democrats, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., have denounced the probe as political persecution of one of President Donald Trump's detractors weeks before a critical election. OBAMA BACKS ILHAN OMAR AMID PROBE, ACCUSES TRUMP ADMIN OF 'APPALLING' TARGETING IN LENGTHY STATEMENT Federal agents raided Omar's Washington, D.C., home earlier this week and took her cellphone and other possessions. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Asked whether the federal government has reason to investigate any type of wrongdoing beyond immigration fraud, Homan said he wouldn't go there. "That's a question for the FBI. I know things, but that's the question for FBI," he said. Fox News Digital reached out to Omar's office for comment but did not immediately hear back. articles.title: GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as Yemen fighting intensifies
articles.summary: Gulf ministers urge action against Houthis as fighting displaces more than 233,000 people across Yemen.
articles.body:
The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has condemned repeated attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi fighters on Saudi Arabia and pledged support for the kingdom.

The political and economic bloc that includes Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates issued a statement on Sunday, shortly after their foreign ministers’ meeting in Manama, Bahrain.

The statement said an attack on any member affected all six, invoking a joint defence agreement and backing Saudi Arabia’s right to protect itself.

The condemnation came as the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis reported shooting down two drones near Riyadh and in Saudi Arabia ‘s Eastern Province early on Sunday.

The coalition said another drone had been intercepted near the capital hours earlier, but did not identify who launched it.

Gulf ministers accused the Houthis of carrying out deadly strikes on civilian airports and vital facilities.

They also pressed for tighter enforcement of a United Nations arms embargo against the group and urged countries to formally designate it “a terrorist organisation”.

The ministers welcomed an October 15 statement from the UN Security Council (UNSC), the body responsible for maintaining international peace, which condemned Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and threats to Red Sea shipping.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government separately appealed to the UNSC to act against Houthi attacks on homes and state facilities.

In letters addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the UNSC’s president for October, Aglaia Balta, the Yemeni government cited an attack on the presidential palace in Aden, where the government is temporarily based.

Separately on Sunday, UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud in Abu Dhabi to discuss regional security, the UAE’s state news agency WAM reported.

Meanwhile, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces press offensives on several fronts.

The Yemeni military said the Houthis fired missiles towards the central city of Marib on Sunday, while government troops reported gains in Taiz, further south.

Government-aligned commanders said eight soldiers died in fighting in Lahij province on Saturday.

Government forces also claimed to have killed 12 Houthi fighters in southern Taiz, figures that could not be independently confirmed.

This latest phase of the war followed Houthi gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast last month.

Government forces launched a counteroffensive intended to recapture territory from the Houthis, who seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

The fighting has uprooted more than 233,000 people, according to the International Organization for Migration, the UN’s migration agency.

About 121,000 are in Taiz province, where supply routes have been disrupted by the fighting.

Al Jazeera’s Hadeel al-Yamani, reporting from Taiz, said cooking gas was unavailable and food stocks were dwindling as Houthi forces blocked supplies through the city’s western entrance.

A local office tracking the siege said food prices had risen fivefold.

The World Health Organization, the UN health agency, warned that Taiz’s 12 hospitals had fuel for just four more days and had run out of surgical supplies.

Oxygen and medicines were also critically scarce as the city struggled with a cholera outbreak.

articles.title: 3 relatives held for abetment after 5 of family found dead at home
articles.summary: Three relatives arrested in Greater Noida for abetment to suicide after a couple and three children were found dead; phone audio clips point to a property dispute.
articles.body: Noida: Three persons were arrested for abetment to suicide after five members of a family, including three children, were found dead at their home in Greater Noida’s Rabupura on Saturday. Police said four audio recordings recovered from a phone in the house pointed to a property dispute within the family.The five who were found dead – frothing at the mouth – were Mahesh, his wife Lalita (35) and their children Laddu (11), Mishti (7) and Sakshat (3). On Sunday, police arrested Mahesh’s sisters Sunita (45) and Sapna (32), and Sunita’s husband Shekhar (50), all residents of Delhi. They were arrested on charges of abetment to suicide.According to Rabupura SHO Shyambabu Shukla, Sunita allegedly influenced their mother to have the family house transferred in her name in 2025, leaving Mahesh upset. Their mother lived in the same Rabupura house with Mahesh.“Four audio recordings, each around two minutes long, were recovered from Mahesh’s phone. In one, he can be heard blaming Sunita, Shekhar and Sapna for the extreme step. He did not blame his mother, who lived with them,” Shukla said.The recordings, sent from one phone to another, helped establish the family dispute and led to the arrests, police said.The sequence of events on Friday night is also central to the probe. Police examined CCTV footage near the house and found that Lalita had gone to a local fair with two children and some neighbours, while Mahesh stayed home with their son. She returned at 10.04pm.Police suspect that after she came back, Lalita prepared noodles for the family and Mahesh may have mixed a poisonous substance into it. The family ate and went to sleep, but none woke up the next morning. Used utensils were found in the house.The deaths came to light around 8am on Saturday, when a boy from the neighbourhood went to call the school-going children for an examination. When nobody answered to repeated knocks on the door, the child climbed over the boundary wall and opened the gate. The child’s mother then entered and found the family unresponsive.Mahesh and one child were on a cot. Lalita and the other two children were on a bed, with one child clinging to her lap. All five, police said, were frothing at the mouth, with no visible injuries.Police said the main gate was bolted from inside and CCTV checks showed no outsider entering the house. However, autopsies did not establish the cause of death. Viscera samples were preserved for forensic analysis.Food poisoning was initially suspected as reason for the deaths because the family had eaten noodles together and drunk tea before bed. But a preliminary inspection by food safety officials did not conclusively establish this as the cause. articles.title: Russia’s war on Ukraine ‘must be brought to an end’, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: Ukraine’s president says communication between Washington and Kyiv ‘virtually nonstop’, despite a spat with Trump.
articles.body:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the war with Russia “must be brought to an end” and that his country is preparing for the “next steps” of diplomacy to end the conflict.

Zelenskyy said on X on Sunday that he had a “conversation with the American president’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner”. He added that “a lot depends” on the US position, but it’s clear there are “many things that matter to all of us”.

The Ukrainian leader’s comments come amid a significant diplomatic fallout with US President Donald Trump, who on Saturday waived expected sanctions targeting Russia’s energy economy and previously called renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure “a disgrace”.

Nonetheless, Zelenskyy said his team is in “virtually nonstop communication” with their US counterparts and said a focus of dialogue is on the results of the talks in Florida and further steps.

Also on Sunday, Zelenskyy said he was “thankful” that the US had resumed intelligence sharing with Ukraine after a pause left Ukraine particularly vulnerable to Russia’s regular ballistic missile attacks.

“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side,” Zelenskyy told NBC, adding: “Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days”.

Kyiv has also reported restrictions on the speed of satellite service Starshield, a military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite connectivity network, provided to Ukraine by Musk’s company SpaceX.

Ukraine said its relays were experiencing a limit on how fast receivers could travel while maintaining connectivity, making it almost impossible to intercept Russia’s upgraded jet-powered long-range drones.

Musk had said any restrictions imposed on Starshield connectivity were the responsibility of the US government. The White House quickly rebuked that and in an NBC interview on Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Zelenskyy “very reckless” for accusing the US of throttling connectivity.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that Ukraine is currently blocked from Starshield, and that a request from Kyiv to access the system for attacks deep inside Russia is “under discussion”.

Also on Sunday, Ukrainian media reported that Russian strikes killed two people in the western Volyn region, near the border with Poland, and injured at least five others across the country. Overnight attacks by Russia killed a woman and injured a six-year-old in the Zaporizhzhia region.

On Saturday night and in the early hours of Sunday, Ukraine hit Russia’s second-largest city, St Petersburg , with a significant drone attack. It targeted a key oil refinery and depot, a warehouse of Russian online retailer Ozon and a data centre run by Russian social media company, VKontakte.

At least one person was killed in the attack, which Russian state media said was the largest on the city since the start of the war in 2022.

articles.title: Macron calls for calm in France and warns rioting must not escalate
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.
articles.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday.

In a national address from the Élysée Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame."

Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted".

Police have arrested about 2,400 people, according to France's interior ministry.

The French president said "nothing justifies" the "unbridled" violence seen and said those involved would face justice.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

On Sunday, looting and clashes with police continued on a smaller scale in parts of the capital and Lyon.

Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people in Paris, according to the AFP news agency, and bottles and rocks were again hurled at police.

Sunday saw cities across the country confront the impact of what developed into one of the worst bouts of disorder in modern French history.

In Limoges, the ornate 19th Century city hall was gutted by a fire started by rioters on Saturday, its clock tower and roof collapsing and the flames took hold.

Speaking near the ruined building, Annèyse said: "This is very upsetting. Harming heritage buildings just because you are angry at the government is selfish, I think. It's hurting everybody."

"It's awful and unbelievable," said another man who gave his name as Gerrard. "We are very sad and I think it will be a long time to put it back as it was before."

Shopkeepers were seen early on Sunday morning picking up large shards of glass in Paris as rubbish trucks cleared up debris on some of the larger streets.

Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas.

Macron said local prefects and mayors would draft measures to protect shops and civic buildings.

The president also said there would be "full transparency" over the police response to the demonstrations.

Tear gas and water cannon were turned on crowds over the weekend and riot police were seen hitting people with batons in several places.

France's interior ministry said about 1,000 police officers were injured on Saturday, seven of them seriously.

Student protests which began last month escalated significant on Saturday after they were joined by trade union members and other anti-government groups.

The response from political figures has pointed to France's deep political divisions as the country prepares for an election in April which could see the hard-right pitted against the hard-left.

France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that while demonstrating was a fundamental right, there were "outrages" committed by "several thousand far-left individuals" who were determined to target public buildings and confront the police.

Later, they were joined by "delinquents who looted and ransacked numerous businesses in several cities in France", he said.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon - leader of the hard-left La France Insoumise party - heavily criticised Nuñez and police chiefs on social media.

He said they had "shown complete incompetence" with their handling of the demonstrations and called them "specialists in organised chaos".

Meanwhile, the leader of the hard-right National Rally party, Marine Le Pen, condemned the "exploitation" of anger "by political forces that encourage violence".

articles.title: Week 7 AP Top 25 Poll features a complete shuffle after chaotic weekend, with Miami taking over the top spot
articles.summary: Miami claims the No. 1 spot, BYU rises to No. 2, and Ohio State sits third after five Top 10 teams fell in a chaotic Week 7 AP Top 25 shakeup.
articles.body: Week 7 of the 2026 college football season will go down as one of the most chaotic ever, with five Top 10 teams suffering losses, and the newest AP Top 25 Poll reflects the craziness that unfolded. For the first time this season, not one team in the AP Poll remained in the same spot it found itself ranked the week prior. We've also got a fresh new Top 3 teams in the country, with Miami taking over the No. 1 spot, followed by BYU at No. 2 and Ohio State sitting in third. When it comes to the biggest jump in the poll, that would belong to the Florida Gators at No. 20 after moving up 12 spots from a week ago. BYU received 20 first-place votes compared to Miami's 40, after moving to 6-0 with its win over No. 2 Notre Dame, 28-24. BYU QB BEAR BACHMEIER SAYS NOTRE DAME 'DISRESPECTED' HIM AND HIS FAMILY FOLLOWING UPSET WIN OVER IRISH Looking at the nine SEC teams ranked in this week's poll, perhaps the biggest head-scratcher involves Kentucky. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 with a win at Oklahoma, which marks their third road win in the conference. articles.title: Indiana father left his entire estate to his fiancee; his daughter challenged the will, lost in court, was ordered to pay $22,208 in legal fees and now faces additional appellate fees
articles.summary: An Indiana woman who challenged her father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her case and now faces a growing legal bill.
articles.body: An Indiana woman who challenged her father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her case and now faces a growing legal bill. According to the court document, Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208.18 in attorney fees after failing to prove that her father's will was invalid. On Wednesday, the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld that decision and ordered her to pay additional fees for the appeal. The final amount of those extra charges has yet to be determined.At the centre of the dispute was Larry Davis, who died in 2022 at the age of 79. In a will signed nearly two years before his death, Larry had decided that everything he owned would go to his fiancee, Michelle Tressler. The couple had been living together since 2012.The decision meant his three adult children, Sherry, Scott and Stacia, would receive nothing unless Tressler died before him. She was still alive when Larry died, leaving her entitled to inherit his estate under the will.Stacia questioned whether her father had made that decision freely and with a clear understanding of what he was signing. Her challenge began a lengthy court dispute.What happened after daughter challenged will?Following Larry's death in 2022, the court accepted the will and appointed Tressler to manage his estate. Stacia challenged it the following month, claiming her father might not have been mentally capable of making a will and raised allegations of pressure and fraud.The case eventually reached a hearing in February 2025, when the court heard from Stacia, Tressler and two women whose signatures appeared on the will.Both witnesses confirmed that the signatures were genuine. Although neither could remember all the details of the signing, their testimony supported the document's validity.Another document presented during the hearing created problems for Stacia's case. It was an affidavit that appeared to come from one of the witnesses and questioned whether she had witnessed the signing. However, the woman told the court that the signature on the affidavit was not hers.Stacia said the document had arrived unexpectedly by post and that she did not know who had sent it. The lower court nevertheless found the affidavit fraudulent and criticised her decision to continue pursuing the case.The court also found that she had not provided acceptable evidence proving her father was mentally incapable of making the will or that Tressler had forced or improperly influenced his decision.How did the inheritance dispute turn into a $22,208 bill?The challenge did not only concern who would inherit Larry's property. It also affected the process of managing what he had left behind.In July 2024, the court removed Tressler from responsibility for the estate after finding delays in its administration. Attorney Robert W. York was appointed to take over as special administrator.As the dispute continued, legal expenses increased. The lower court recorded 431 entries across the two connected cases and found that much of the prolonged litigation was linked to Stacia's actions.Judges also criticised requests for documents that had added to the expenses without producing useful evidence for the case.When the lower court rejected Stacia's challenge in 2025, it decided that she should personally bear part of the legal costs rather than leaving the estate to pay everything.York had sought $26,198.61 in attorney fees. After examining the expenses, the court ordered Stacia to pay $22,208.18. The remaining amount was to be paid from the estate.Stacia challenged this order as well, but the appeals court found that the lower court had sufficient grounds to make her pay.Why did the appeal make matters worse for the daughter?Stacia had been represented by a lawyer during the earlier proceedings but handled her appeal herself. Her submissions created another set of problems.The appeals court found that she had included documents that had never been accepted as evidence during the original hearing. Her written arguments also failed to provide several required references to the court records.The judges identified a more serious issue involving the legal cases she cited to support her arguments. Some of those cases did not exist at the references she provided, while others were real but unrelated to the points she was making. Despite these problems, the court chose to consider her arguments.The judges ultimately agreed with the earlier decision that Larry's will was valid. They also upheld the order requiring Stacia to pay $22,208.18.However, the court went further. It found that her appeal involved serious problems with both the arguments and the way the case had been presented, justifying another award of attorney fees. The case has now been returned to the lower court to calculate how much Stacia must pay for the appeal.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Aretha Franklin bought Detroit’s Rose Estate in 1994, but it later sat boarded up and sold for $300,000 after her death; new owners have since invested more than $2 million restoring the historic home
articles.summary: Behind the boarded windows of a once-grand Detroit mansion lay more than years of neglect.
articles.body: Behind the boarded windows of a once-grand Detroit mansion lay more than years of neglect. The house had witnessed the private life of Aretha Franklin, the Queen of Soul, and belonged to a chapter of the city’s cultural history that risked fading away. Today, the Rose Estate is finding its way back to life, thanks to two new owners determined to preserve its architectural beauty and the stories held within its walls, states an online report by the USA TODAY.According to the March 2025 report, since acquiring the historic property, Detroit residents Trevor Thomas and Brandon Lynum have invested more than $2 million in an ambitious restoration, turning a deteriorating mansion into a tribute to two remarkable women. Scroll down to read the details of the shift of the ownership.A home with a remarkable pastBuilt in 1927, the 5,623-square-foot Tudor-style house sits in the leafy Palmer Woods neighbourhood, overlooking the ninth hole of the Detroit Golf Club. Before Franklin purchased it in March 1994, the property belonged to Patricia Hill Burnett, a portrait artist, feminist advocate and former Miss America runner-up, explains the online report.Burnett's artistic career brought her into contact with some of the most prominent figures of her time. Her portraits included Rosa Parks, Betty Ford, Margaret Thatcher and Ruth Bader Ginsburg, adds the report.Franklin, who already owned a primary residence in Bloomfield Hills, chose the house as a second home and a place to entertain. Its spacious interiors and distinctive architectural details suited her taste for grand gatherings. She retained much of the original character while adding personal touches, including gold sconces, a purple-tinted chandelier and a striking red acrylic bathtub.Years of neglectAccording to As Franklin's health deteriorated, the property gradually fell into disrepair. Its windows were eventually boarded up, and years of water damage took a heavy toll on the interiors. Wildlife also found its way inside, leaving behind additional damage.Following Franklin's death in 2018, her estate sold the house for $300,000 to a Michigan developer. By the time Thomas and Lynum purchased it in June 2023, the restoration required substantial work.The couple, who had previously renovated two homes, approached the project with an understanding that this was no ordinary property. They researched its history through old newspaper clippings, archival material at the University of Michigan and original documents discovered in a concealed compartment in the house's library.Restoring the detailsThe first phase of the restoration has focused on preserving the mansion's original features. Limestone-framed windows, hardwood floors and decorative plasterwork have been carefully revived, while distinctive elements such as Detroit-made Pewabic tiles have retained their place in the house.If we go by the report of USA TODAY, the project has involved nearly 50 contractors, craftsmen and workers. Thomas and Lynum plan to continue restoring the property over the next five years, with further work expected on the slate roof, third floor and basement, which suffered extensive water damage.Alongside the physical restoration, the couple have created a space that celebrates the home's former residents. Photographs, museum-style displays and memorabilia honour both Franklin and Burnett, including a signed Andy Warhol print, outfits from the biopic Respect and a gold-record plaque for Franklin's 1998 album A Rose Is Still a Rose.More than a mansionThe restored Rose Estate is already welcoming nonprofit events, school groups and visitors drawn by Franklin's legacy. For some, the experience is deeply personal, reflecting not only her music but also her commitment to civil rights and women's empowerment, explains the online report.Images Courtesy: Rent Like a Champion and WikipediaReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed invokes JFK to dismiss 'crazy' questions over family's alleged ties to Muslim Brotherhood
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed compared himself to John F. Kennedy, likening Muslim Brotherhood scrutiny to the Catholic faith questions JFK faced in 1960s.
articles.body: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed compared himself to former President John F. Kennedy during a Saturday "MS NOW Reports" interview with Ali Velshi, likening questions about his family's alleged Muslim Brotherhood ties to scrutiny Kennedy faced over his Catholic faith. El-Sayed invoked Kennedy's 1960 presidential campaign while arguing that questions about his family were intended to cast doubt on his allegiance to the United States. "I also know that I tread a long history of this: when John F. Kennedy ran for president, he was asked about whether or not his allegiance would be to the Constitution or to the pope and the Vatican…" he began. "The Constitution guarantees me the right as I choose to pray or any of us, to pray as we choose to pray or not to pray at all," he continued. "Nobody understands how important that document is like somebody who has their rights constantly threatened and so I will stand for that constitution. And it's a crazy thing to assume that somehow I'd have dual loyalties as somebody who's avidly running to protect the right to choose, who's running to protect LGBTQ rights, who's running to protect religious freedom…" EL-SAYED ASKED IF HE BELIEVES AMERICA IS 'READY FOR A MUSLIM PRESIDENT' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE Ted Goodman, communications director of the Michigan GOP, pushed back on El-Sayed's comparison in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing that the allegations involving the Democrat's relatives were fundamentally different from the religious scrutiny Kennedy faced. "Abdul El-Sayed’s comparison of scrutiny over his Muslim Brotherhood ties to the questions JFK faced about the Vatican is a false equivalence," Goodman said. "The Catholic Church and the Muslim Brotherhood are not analogous." "The actual evidence against Abdul El-Sayed is not hearsay based on his faith, but actual facts as reported by numerous reputable news outlets," he continued. Velshi asked El-Sayed how he responded to questions involving the Muslim Brotherhood, terrorism and radical Islamism. El-Sayed suggested the scrutiny was designed to raise doubts about his loyalty. "Look, at the end of the day, the whole reason this question is being asked is to insinuate that somehow I have dual loyalties," he said. ABDUL EL-SAYED HITS BACK AT ISRAEL QUESTIONS, SUGGESTS HIS NAME AND FAITH ARE BEHIND PRESS SCRUTINY The controversy followed reporting on social media posts uncovered by the Washington Free Beacon in which El-Sayed's half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, described her family's history with the Muslim Brotherhood. In one 2012 post, Abdelhadi described a conversation with her and El-Sayed's mother, Fatten Elkomy, about her involvement with the organization during college in Egypt. "Had an amazing talk with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood during the early 70s while she was in college #respect." ABDUL EL-SAYED PROTESTED AGAINST 'EX-TERRORISTS' WHO CONVERTED TO CHRISTIANITY, UNEARTHED REPORT REVEALS In another post, Abdelhadi characterized her family's history with the organization. "My family has long been MB, but I've always felt that it has navigated the political sphere poorly/destructively." El-Sayed previously denied that he or his family had ties to the organization during an Oct. 11 appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press." Days later, he was pressed by NBC's Tom Llamas about his half-sister's statements and whether he had discussed the allegations with his mother. El-Sayed maintained that he had no personal connections to the group and disputed the significance of his sister's posts. "I have never had these conversations with my mother. I wasn’t raised by my mother..." he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Goodman cited El-Sayed's father-in-law, Tayeb Jukaku, whose involvement with the Islamic Society of North America and CAIR's Michigan chapter was documented by the Washington Free Beacon. The outlet also reported that Jukaku contributed $200,000 to a super PAC supporting El-Sayed. The organization was named as an unindicted co-conspirator in the Holy Land Foundation terrorism-financing case. The Treasury Department designated the Egyptian and Jordanian branches of the Muslim Brotherhood as Specially Designated Global Terrorists in January for providing material support to Hamas. The allegations involving El-Sayed's relatives have not established that he personally belonged to the organization. El-Sayed's campaign previously rejected accusations involving his family in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing Republican opponent Mike Rogers of using the controversy to attack his faith. "Independent fact-checkers have repeatedly debunked Mike’s lies, but their campaign continues to use bad faith attacks on Abdul's faith and family," the campaign said. articles.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
articles.summary: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.
articles.body:
Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him. "We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."

The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California. Police said officials are investigating his death as a suspected overdose.

Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

Crawford wrote in the post on Sunday: "We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years."

"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," she also posted.

"Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia," she wrote in closing, with an emoji of angel wings.

The tribute also listed the dates of his birth and death.

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner lists Gerber's case as pending additional investigation. The Santa Monica Police Department has said there is no indication foul play was involved in his death.

Gerber's sister Kaia also dedicated a post to him on Sunday which included a video of the two siblings as children dancing together, a photo of them standing near the ocean, and a four-page letter to "prez" typed out on a blue background.

In the letter, she said she had been scared of getting her ears pierced, so "you went first".

"But when I held the earring they took from your body, all I could think was: That belongs to you," she wrote.

"I am learning how to love you when I cannot see you," she also wrote. "How to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you. How to be your sister in a world that I can't reach for you in," she wrote.

In recent years, Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use and frequently posted videos on Instagram himself for what he called "Mental Health Mondays".

His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.

articles.title: Colorado neighbors used a shared private easement to reach their homes; after a solar developer planned power lines through it for a separate project, a judge blocked that use and barred trespass on one family’s land
articles.summary: A shared road meant to provide access to neighbouring properties has become the centre of a legal battle in Colorado, where a dispute over a solar
articles.body: A shared road meant to provide access to neighbouring properties has become the centre of a legal battle in Colorado, where a dispute over a solar development has raised questions about property rights, utility infrastructure and the limits of private easements. According to a report by The Business Times, a judge has now stepped in, restricting how a solar developer and other defendants can use the route while the lawsuit continues.The ruling in Mesa County draws a distinction between accessing land that has rights under the easement and using the same route to serve a separate solar project that does not, adds the online report.A shared road, competing interestsAs per The Business Times report, the dispute centres on an easement providing access to James Sterling’s property at 656 39 Road, outside Palisade, where Pivot Energy has leased land for a solar development. The report explains that Sterling entered into solar and battery-storage leases with Pivot in December 2022. The company subsequently entered agreements with Xcel Energy to connect solar facilities to the electrical grid, while Sturgeon Electric Company was contracted to install utility infrastructure.The conflict arose over plans to install power lines within the shared easement to serve the separate Summy Solar Project, located south of the neighbouring properties. If we go by the court’s findings, the Summy property has no rights under the easement.In a preliminary injunction issued on September 25, Mesa County District Judge JenniLynn E. Lawrence prohibited the defendants from using the easement to benefit the Summy project, including installing the proposed power lines. Access to Sterling’s property through the designated route remains permitted, the online report explains.Neighbours take the dispute to courtAnother report by The Grand Junction Source states that the lawsuit was filed on April 17 by James and Christine Murphy, Raven Novak, Cullen and Krista Howard, and James and Maureen Delany. The defendants include Sterling, Pivot Energy Development LLC, Pivot Solar 44 LLC, Sturgeon Electric Company and Public Service Company of Colorado, which operates as Xcel Energy.The court had previously issued a temporary restraining order in April before holding an evidentiary hearing on September 4.The judge found that the landowners had established a reasonable probability of prevailing on their claim that the easement could not legally be used to benefit the Summy property. The injunction is intended to protect their property rights while the broader dispute proceeds.The order does not prohibit solar development in the surrounding area. Instead, it addresses the permitted use of the specific easement and the defendants’ conduct on neighbouring land.Trespassing and road safety concernsAccording to the report, the ruling also addresses a shortcut across the northeast corner of the Howards’ property, outside the designated easement. The route had historically been used with the owners’ permission, but that permission was withdrawn after its use intensified. The Howards subsequently posted no-trespassing signs.According to the judge’s findings, video evidence showed the defendants or their employees crossing the property before the shortcut was roped off. The injunction now prohibits the defendants from trespassing on the Howards’ land, including by using the unauthorised route.And, road safety is another concern. The court found that Sterling had removed substantial amounts of soil along the easement road, leaving vertical cuts measuring eight to 10 feet. The resulting loose, unsecured slopes could wash onto the road and potentially destabilise nearby power poles.Sterling has been prohibited from creating further unsafe conditions, including additional vertical cuts that leave unstable slopes, the online report mentions.Legal battle far from overAs per the report, Pivot and Sterling argue that the easement permits access and utility-related uses connected with Sterling’s property, including solar development. They also maintain that the agreement does not require neighbouring owners to approve reasonable improvements.Xcel denies wrongdoing and argues that the agreement allows electrical distribution lines to be installed. Alternatively, the utility says it may pursue additional property rights through condemnation, a legal process through which private property can be acquired for qualifying public uses with compensation. Sturgeon also denies wrongdoing, negligence and trespassing.The judge's order makes clear that the availability of condemnation does not, by itself, authorise a utility to use an easement without a legal right to do so.The preliminary injunction does not settle the underlying claims. A seven-day trial is scheduled to begin on September 27, 2027, with further proceedings planned through October 5. Until then, the ruling establishes boundaries on access, construction and property use as the legal fight continues, the report states.Images Courtesy: istockYou use AI every day.
